title: Sprint deployment playpad — zen brief
content:
Sprint deployment playpad — zen brief

Purpose:
- Compact, action-first guide for the 2027-03 sprint release. Designed for a small ops squad (2x on-call + 1x release lead) to run a low-latency model rollout with minimal interruption. Treat as the single source-of-truth during the 6-hour window.

Audience:
- release engineer oncall, serving-runtime, SRE, product release lead, solutions eng on call for large customers.

High-level running plan (mar 18, 2027, UTC):
- 08:00 — Preflight (30m): final smoke, metrics snapshot, traffic baseline capture.
- 08:30 — Canary start (10% traffic, 3 instances): observe 0–30m.
- 09:00 — Canary health review (15m): if green -> ramp to 30%.
- 09:30 — Ramp to 60% (observe 30m).
- 10:00 — Ramp to 100% if no regressions, else hold and triage.
- 12:00 — Post-deploy stabilization review and signoff.

Primary contacts (in order):
- Release lead: Asha Patel (Slack: @asha.p)
- SRE lead: Evan Cho (@evan.c)
- Serving runtime: Diego Ramirez (@diego.r)
- Escalation: Priya Nair (PM) (@priya.n)

Runway essentials (quick-check list) — quick tick before 08:00:
- [ ] PRs merged and CI green (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/core/pull/4578).
- [ ] Deployment artifact baked and scanned for secrets.
- [ ] Canary pool configured in infra (3 instances, isolation tag: sprint-mar-2027).
- [ ] Route policy ready (traffic weights and fallback).
- [ ] Observability dashboards preloaded and pinned.
- [ ] Pager/rotation confirmed for next 6 hours.
- [ ] Shared doc pinned in #release-ops and #sre-shift.

Detailed preflight (check during 08:00 window):
- Telemetry snapshot: 1h baseline for p50/p95 latency, error-rate, token cost. Capture values to artifacts: p50_latency, p95_latency, 5xx_rate, request_rate.
- Canary smoke tests: short scripted prompts, long prompts (2k tokens), multi-turn chat simulation. Expected: coherent output, no OOMs, tail latency within baseline +20%.
- KV cache warmup check: ensure warmup scripts executed against canary nodes. Cache hit ratio target >= 80% after warmup.
- Autoscaler sanity: simulated spike test (x3 reqs for 60s) to validate scale-up.
- Circuit-breaker config: verify fallback model id and region fallback list.

Canary policy and gates:
- Canary period: 30 minutes per stage unless a gate fires.
- Health gates (any triggers cause pause/rollback):
  - 5xx rate > baseline + 0.5% sustained for 5m.
  - p95 latency > baseline * 2 for 5m.
  - Error budget burn rate > 3x expected.
  - Any OOMs or GPU preemption observed.
  - Serving node crashloop or gRPC stream failures > 3 nodes in 10m.
- Soft alerts (review required but may not block): minor regressions in quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE decline > 5%) or small increases in token cost.

Ramp schedule (percent traffic):
- Stage A: 10% (08:30–09:00) — baseline smoke
- Stage B: 30% (09:00–09:30) — midpoint review
- Stage C: 60% (09:30–10:00) — high-load observe
- Stage D: 100% (post-10:00) — monitor 2 hours closely

Rollforward vs rollback rules (fast decision criteria):
- Rollforward (preferred if transient issue resolved and root not in serving code): continue ramp with increased monitoring and create follow-up ticket.
- Rollback (immediate revert to previous model variant): any of the health gates firing, major customer impact signals, or unresolved memory leaks. Use infra rollback play: route weight back to previous model id and scale previous pool.

Rollback procedure (quick):
- Call out on #release-ops: "Immediate rollback — reason: <short reason>".
- Execute: route update -> previous-model -> 100%; scale previous pool to target; scale new pool to 0.
- Post-action: capture heap dumps/logs, open incident ticket JIRA-XXXX-rollback.

Observability and queries to run (prometheus / tracing / logs):
- latency_p50, latency_p95 (by model_id) — compare to baseline tags.
- http_5xx_rate (by route) — alert threshold 0.5% absolute above baseline.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio (by node) — expect > 80% within 10m of warmup.
- gpu_mem_free, gpu_oom_events (node exporter) — immediate red.
- trace sample: slow-path traces (> p95) with stackframe to kernel op.

Customer signposting & comms:
- Pre-announce to large customers with scheduled maintenance window: 48h notice sent by solutions-eng.
- If rollback: email template (short) and dedicated bridge.
- Release notes (short draft below) publish to internal release notes channel after stabilization.

Draft release notes (internal first):
- Headline: "March sprint: optimized KV caching + model runtime patch"
- Summary: "Reduced p95 decoding latency for long-context prompts by ~12% in internal benchmarks and improved cache reuse across concurrent chat sessions. Includes a fix for rare memory leak on long chat tails."
- Impact: "No expected breaking changes to API. Rolling update across serving fleet."
- Rollout: "Canary -> staged ramp -> full rollout. Contact release lead for questions."

Post-deploy checklist (first 4 hours):
- [ ] Confirm no major regressions on p95/p50 and 5xx.
- [ ] Validate top 5 customer flows (synth scripts) for quality regressions.
- [ ] Snapshot token cost and compare to projections.
- [ ] Export telemetry snapshot for post-release review.

24–72h follow-up items:
- Run quality evals against held prompt-set (automated) and record delta.
- If regressions > threshold, schedule immediate patch sprint.
- Add any observed flaky test cases to CI-matrix.
- Schedule postmortem if rollback occurred or if any health gates fired.

Unresolved questions / notes to self:
- Do we need a dark-launch for a subset of customers? Tradeoffs: faster validation vs complexity of segmented routing.
- Consider adding a mid-canary synthetic generator for long-tail prompts (next sprint).
- Re-evaluate cache warmup sequence — observed 10% slower warmup in staging last run.

Ops haiku (for morale):
- quiet pager at dawn
- traffic folds into steady hum
- coffee and a ping

Quick links (pin these during the window):
- Dashboards: https://telemetry.redwood.com/dashboards/sprint-mar-2027
- Deployment console: https://deploy.redwood.com/releases/2027-03-sprint
- Incident template: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Incident-Template

Last edits: Asha Patel — 2027-03-08 (draft).

TODO (before finalizing):

- [ ] Add staged traffic annotations to observability dashboard. (Diego)

End of playpad.
